text.p: Shareholders of French insurers Axa and UAP overwhelmingly approved on Monday the merger of the two companies, creating the world's second largest insurer.

The vote at a shareholder's meeting eliminated the last legal hurdle to the operation announced last November. The merger, which Axa had called "the deal of the century," is retroactive to January 1, 1997.
"It's very encouraging," Claude Bebear, chief executive of the new group, told reporters after the vote. "Now we must get down to work to complete the synergies we said would happen."
"Our ambition is to focus on our core businesses - insurance and financial services," he said.
The new group's holding company name will be Axa-UAP while the brand name worldwide will be Axa. Axa now holds 91.39 percent of UAP shares.
The two companies have been integrating their operations since the announcement of the 40 billion franc ($7 billion) deal that involved the swap of five UAP shares for two of Axa-UAP.

The new group is studying its foreign operations to see which areas can be merged. It said a decision would be taken by the summer on the future of Sun Life and Equity and Law, the two British insurance subsidiaries owned by Axa-UAP.

Axa-UAP is reported to be reviewing whether to merge Equity and Law with Sun Life and Provincial or sell it. It is said to be leaning more toward merging the two businesses because it wants to retain a large presence in Britain.
In Spain, the group is looking at merging its three companies there. It is also looking at how it can streamline its eight Italian companies and expects to make a decision before year end.

Bebear, who has said the new group will be able to achieve cost savings of around one billion francs by 1999 through eliminating overlapping activities, reiterated it was aiming for a return on equity of 11 percent from 1998 and 15 percent by the year 2001 or 2002, up from 10.2 percent in 1996.

Axa insisted when the surprise deal was announced it was a "friendly operation between equals." But analysts said it was clear highly profitable Axa was taking over formerly state-owned UAP, which was hard hit by the French property slump.
Over the past two decades, Bebear has guided Axa from a sleepy mutual insurance company into an acquisitive powerhouse.

Two years ago, Axa bought Australian life insurer National Mutual, acquiring a springboard for Asian expansion. Earlier in the decade it established a strong foothold in the United States with the purchase of insurer Equitable Cos.

AXA-UAP will have combined turnover of 340 billion francs. making it the second largest insurer after Nippon Life of Tokyo. It will also be the world's second largest insurer in terms of managed assets after Fidelity of the United States.

Separately, Axa-UAP reported first-quarter consolidated revenues rose 11.0 percent to 98.66 billion francs from 88.92 billion. On a like-for-like basis, revenues rose 6.1 percent. ($ = 5.681 French Francs)
